$comment: R1832 — the analysis tool's DEFERRED REGISTER, written down once, in
neutral vocabulary, as the behaviour reference states it.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Several surfaces of this application show a seat that
is drawn but locked, and each one tells the reader WHICH requirement will
fill it. That number is the only thing the screen says about what is
coming, so a wrong one is a false statement to a reader — and until this
file there was nothing to check one against. The rail's two locked seats
carried their numbers in a `$note` (prose, unchecked) and the palette's
locked widgets carried theirs only in the Rust table.
WHAT `where` MEANS. The reference exposes a deferred capability in one of
three ways, and it says which for every one of them:
palette   — a locked seat in the dashboard's widget palette
rail      — a locked seat in the navigation rail
in-place  — foreshadowed inside a screen this build already has
console   — deferred to a separate console that does not exist yet
★★★★★ THE DEBT THAT PRODUCED THIS FILE HAD ITS DIAGNOSIS BACKWARDS, and
the entry re-measurement is what found it. It recorded that the reference
defers SIX requirements and that `admin`'s citation of 14 was therefore
wrong. Measured: the reference defers FIFTEEN (12 through 26) and says so
in one sentence; the six it had read are the six the PALETTE caption
happens to enumerate. 14 is a real deferred requirement — the admin query —
so the citation it called a defect is correct. Every palette and rail
citation in the tree is correct, which is what this file now holds them to.
WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than left as an absence: the two key
rows on the settings screen cite requirements this register books to other
capabilities entirely. That is a real finding and it is NOT repaired here,
because inventing a number would be worse than naming the gap — see
`owed` below and the debt it points at.
Vocabulary is this tree's own throughout. The reference's wording is not
reproduced; what is pinned is the ASSIGNMENT — which number books which
capability — because that is the fact a screen can be wrong about.
★★★★★ ONE REQUIREMENT CAN SURFACE TWICE, and the gate is what taught it.
`deferred[].seat` is the PALETTE seat; `rail` below is a separate list
because the reference exposes requirement 18 on BOTH surfaces — a rail
destination and a widget seat, for one capability. The gate's first draft
asserted the two agreed and failed on exactly that, correctly. So what is
checked across surfaces is that the number is one this register defers at
all; WHICH seat carries it is per-surface.

deferred.books: an active query asking a node about itself
decoding a payload in a user-supplied format
a throughput time series per resource

Built as a placed dashboard card at R1843. The reference places this seat on its DEFAULT board and in four presets, and its catalogue entry for the seat names a sparkline no other widget of that catalogue has. The rail's `sessions` seat cites the same requirement and stays locked, which is why 18 remains in `deferred`.

Built as a placed dashboard card at R1851, on the R1797 / R1843 pattern. The evidence is the reference's own board rather than a preference: it places this seat by default, three of its four built-in presets place it, and its catalogue entry declares the 4x2 footprint this board gives it. What the seat was waiting for was a framework that could draw the thing — a feed is a virtualised list under a sortable column header, and measured the same round nothing in this tree composed those two: counted by file, the virtualised list family had 27 consumers and the column header three, of which one is a screenshot harness and one a shell test - so exactly one screen had ever drawn a column header. The only surface holding both was the data grid, where every row is a row of cells and a severity swatch beside a graded word is not. `pinion_widget_paint::header_feed` is that composition and `pinion_core::widgets::severity` is the ordered vocabulary its threshold reads.
